To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the finite element modeling of the vertebra can be used to predict the changes of stress and strain within the vertebra during osteoporotic fracture.
The finite element model was created with the geometry and material properties of the vertebra retrieved from CT scan.
the stress distribution in the vertebral body is affected by the bone mineral density, the geometry of vertebral body and the location of the fracture.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an efficient finite element model of the human lumbar vertebrae, based on CT data, and with the use of this model in prediction of stress distributions within vertebra during different phases of osteopenia.

the development of finite element model of the vertebra, with geometry and material parameters retrieved from CT scan, and with its application in prediction the stress and strain distributions in different phases of the osteoporosis.
the development of a finite element modeling method to predict stress and strain distributions in vertebra with different bone densities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the finite element modeling of the human vertebra is a powerful tool for the analysis of stress and strain distribution in the vertebra and its application in the prediction of vertebral fracture risk.

the finite element modeling of the vertebra with geometry reconstructed from CT scan data is a very promising tool in prediction of stress distribution within vertebra in the different phases of osteoposis.

finite element modeling of the human vertebra is an efficient tool for predicting the stress and strain distribution in the human vertebra and for the prediction of the risk of osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
finite element modeling of the vertebra is possible and it can provide valuable insight into the biomechanics of the spine.

we have successfully developed a method for subject specific finite element model reconstruction of human vertebra with geometry, material properties and boundary conditions retrieved from CT-scan data and applied the method to predict stress and strain distribution within vertebra in normal, early and advanced osteoporosis.
we developed a method for finite element modeling of human vertebra with geometry retrieved from CT scan images and material properties retrieved with an image based approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the finite element model of the vertebra can be reconstructed from CT scan data with a high degree of accuracy.
the finite element modeling of the human spine is possible and that the results obtained from this modeling can be used in the prediction of stress and strains in the spine.

finite element modeling of the vertebra with geometry reconstructed from CT scan data is a viable approach to predict stress and strain distributions and to understand bone remodeling in different stages of osteoporosis and in different phases of treatment.
